# SK1073 — Use the framework's cached instance

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A stateless framework value is constructed where the framework already holds one: `new EventArgs()` is `EventArgs.Empty`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

`new EventArgs()` allocates an object with no state, on an event that may be raised in a loop, where `EventArgs.Empty` is already there. The three struct cases cost nothing at run time and are a readability finding instead: `Guid.Empty`, `TimeSpan.Zero` and `CancellationToken.None` say what the value *is*, where `new Guid()` says only how it was made. Every one of them is a name a model writes the long way round because the long way round is what most of its training data does.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
Changed?.Invoke(this, new EventArgs());
if (id == new Guid()) { }
```

Write:

```csharp
Changed?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty);
if (id == Guid.Empty) { }
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The table is four entries long and every one of them carries its own proof, because "there is a cached instance" is not a property that generalizes.** `EventArgs` has no instance state and no member that could tell one instance from another, so `EventArgs.Empty` and a fresh one differ only by reference identity. `Guid.Empty`, `TimeSpan.Zero` and `CancellationToken.None` are the default value of a struct, where identity is not observable at all. The member is looked up on the resolved type and required to be a static field or property of that same type before anything is reported — a table that assumed the member exists would report a fix that does not compile the day a framework drops one. ⚠ **The zero-length-array half of this concept is deliberately absent: `new T[0]` is `CA1825`, which ships in the SDK, and ADR-008 hosts rather than rebuilds.** ⚠ **A parameter's default value is the trap.** `void M(TimeSpan t = new TimeSpan())` compiles and `= TimeSpan.Zero` does not, because a default must be a compile-time constant and a static readonly field is not one; the same holds for an attribute argument and a constant pattern, and all of them are excluded by position. ⚠ The type must be the framework's: it is resolved by metadata name and required to come from a referenced assembly, so a source type of the same name is never matched. Only a creation with no arguments and no initializer, and only `default(T)` written with its type — a bare `default` takes its type from a context this rule does not re-derive. A target-typed `new()` is not matched either, because there is no written type to build the replacement from; the fix reproduces the type exactly as the file spells it, so an alias or a `using`-shortened name stays spelled that way and no `using` is required that the file does not have. ⚠ `EventArgs.Empty` is a singleton, so code comparing event arguments by reference would see a change — the residual false positive, and the reason the entry is worth stating rather than assuming.
